Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:10:1.hebrew: המבעית - תקע לו באזנו פתאום ובעתו, דלא עבד ביה מעשה בגופו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:10:1.english: One who frightens - He shouted into his ear suddenly and frightened him, for he did not perform an action upon his body.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:11:1.hebrew: ר"מ מחייב בהזיקן - פלוגתייהו מיפרשא בהמניח את הכד (דף כט.), בנתקל פושע ובמפקיר נזקיו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:11:1.english: Rabbi Meir deems [him] liable for their damage - Their dispute is explained in [the chapter] HaMeniach Et HaKad (29a), regarding [whether] one who stumbles is negligent and regarding one who declares his damaging [objects] ownerless.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:15:1.english: I covered it - So that the fire would not burn it quickly.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:16:1.english: One listens to the words of the teacher - And they should not have testified.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:18:1.hebrew: והוא שחתרה - הא דתנן נפרצה בלילה פטור, כגון שחתרה הבהמה והפילה הכותל, דאנוס הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:18:1.english: And [this is] where it tunneled - That which we learned in the Mishnah, "[If] it was breached at night, he is exempt," [is a case] such as where the animal tunneled and knocked down the wall, for [the owner] is [considered] forced by circumstances [beyond his control].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:19:1.english: But [if] it did not tunnel - rather, [the wall] fell on its own.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:19:2.hebrew: תחלתו בפשיעה - שהניחה בחמה, ופשיעה היא אצל פתיחת הדלת, דאמרינן לקמיה: כל תחבולות שיכולה לעשות, עושה אגב צערה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:19:2.english: Initially through negligence - For he left [the animal] in the sun, and that is negligence with respect to opening the door, as we say later: it employs every stratagem it can because of its distress.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:19:3.english: And ultimately by accident - [In] that [the animal] tunneled.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:1:1.hebrew: בכותל רעוע - דלא אפסדיה, דלמסתר קאי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:1:1.english: Of an unstable wall - For he did not cause him [any] loss, since it stands to collapse.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:20:1.hebrew: הניחא למאן דאמר כו' - פלוגתא היא בסוף המפקיד (ב"מ דף מב.), תרי לישני דש"ס אליבא דרב יוסף:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:20:1.english: This works out well according to the one who said, etc. - It is a dispute at the end of [the chapter] HaMafkid (Bava Metzia 42a) — two versions of the Talmud according to Rav Yosef.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:20:2.hebrew: תחילתו בפשיעה - אצל נפילה, דעביד למיפל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:20:2.english: Initially through negligence - With respect to falling, for [the wall] is apt to fall.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:21:1.hebrew: ה"ג - אלא מתני' בכותל בריא, ואפילו לא חתרה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:21:1.english: This is the reading - Rather, the Mishnah [refers] to a sound wall, and even [if] it did not tunnel:

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:21:2.english: Left it in the sun, etc. Rabbah said: And even if it tunneled - And [this applies even] with a sturdy wall.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:22:1.hebrew: תחלתו בפשיעה - שהניחה בחמה, ופשיעה היא אצל פתיחת הדלת, דאמרינן לקמיה: כל תחבולות שיכולה לעשות, עושה אגב צערה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:22:1.english: Initially through negligence - Because he left it in the sun, and it is negligence with respect to opening the door, as we say later: any stratagems that it can employ, it employs because of its distress.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:22:2.english: And ultimately by accident - [In] that it tunneled.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:2:1.english: That [the fire] reaches it - When he bent it, the fire reached it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:2:2.hebrew: ברוח מצויה - הרי בידים הבעיר, ובדיני אדם ניחייב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:2:2.english: In a typical wind - Behold, he burned [it] with his own hands, and by human laws he should be liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:2:3.english: In an atypical wind - Because it is something that does not enter his mind.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:3:1.hebrew: טמון איתמר - שכיסה קמת חבירו בסדינין כשראה דליקה אצלה, והוא לא שלח את הבערה, ושוייה טמון, וגרם להפסיד את הניזק ולפטור את המבעיר, דפטור על טמון באש:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:3:1.english: [It] was stated [regarding] a concealed [item] - That he covered his fellow's standing grain with sheets when he saw a fire near it, and he [himself] did not set the fire, and [thereby] made it a concealed [item], and caused a loss to the injured party and exempted the one who kindled [the fire], for [one] is exempt for a concealed [item] [damaged] by fire.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:4:1.english: For himself - To extract money from his fellow for himself.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:4:2.english: He must pay money - That money that he extracted, he is obligated to return.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:4:3.english: For another - He hired false witnesses to extract a maneh from Reuven for Shimon.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:5:1.english: It is obvious; it is by Torah law - That he is liable under the laws of Heaven.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:5:2.hebrew: אם לא יגיד - בתרי קא משתעי; מדקפיד אהגדה, משמע שאילו מגידין מתחייב זה ממון. ועוד, קי"ל (סוטה דף ב:): כל מקום שנאמר עד, הרי כאן שני עדים, עד שיפרט לך הכתוב אחד, כדכתיב "לא יקום עד אחד באיש" (דברים י״ט:ט״ו):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:5:2.english: If he does not utter it - [The verse] is speaking of two [witnesses]; since it is particular about [their] telling [the testimony], it implies that if they were to testify, this [defendant] would become liable [to pay] money. Furthermore, we hold (Sotah 2b) [that] wherever "witness" is stated, two witnesses are [meant] here, unless Scripture specifies "one" for you, as it is written: "One witness shall not rise up against a man" (Deuteronomy 19:15).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:6:1.hebrew: אלא בחד - שמחייבו שבועה, ובדיני שמים מיחייב, דאי הוה מסהיד מחייב ליה שבועה, ודלמא לא הוי משתבע בשיקרא ומשלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:6:1.english: Rather, [with] a single [witness] - Who obligates him [to take] an oath, and he is liable under the laws of Heaven; for if he had testified, he would have obligated him [to take] an oath, and perhaps he would not have sworn falsely and [thus] would have paid.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:7:1.english: And are there no more - [cases] that are liable by the laws of Heaven.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:7:2.hebrew: העושה מלאכה במי חטאת - ששקל כנגדן משקלות, במסכת גיטין (דף נג.), והן נפסלין במלאכה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:7:2.english: One who performs labor with water of purification - [Such as] where he weighed weights against them, [as taught] in Tractate Gittin (53a), and they become disqualified through labor.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:7:3.hebrew: פטור מדיני אדם - דהיזק שאינו ניכר לא שמיה היזק. וכולהו הני תיובתי מתנייתא נינהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 56a:7:3.english: Exempt according to human laws - Because damage that is not discernible is not considered damage. And all these refutations are baraitot.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:12:1.hebrew: אבל הני אצטריך ליה - וא"ת: הנותן סם המות נמי חידוש הוא למיתני, כדאמרינן לעיל (בבא קמא דף מז:) דאפילו סם המות דלא עבידא דאכלה חייב בדיני שמים? ושמא אין כל כך חידוש:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:12:1.english: But these [cases] were necessary for him - And if you ask: [The case of] one who places deadly poison [before his neighbor's animal] is also a novelty to teach, as we say earlier (Bava Kamma 47b) that even [with] deadly poison, which [the animal] does not usually eat, he is liable according to the laws of Heaven? Perhaps [that case] is not so much of a novelty.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:15:1.hebrew: כסויי כסיתיה - וא"ת, גלוי וידוע למקום למה נתכוין, אם לטובה אם לרעה. וי"ל, דאפי' במתכוין לטובה — שלא ימהר לשרוף, ויוכל להציל בעל הבית בתוך כך — מ"מ בדיני שמים חייב, דאיבעי ליה לאזדהורי ולאסוקי אדעתיה שלא יבא לו הפסד בכך:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:15:1.english: "I covered it" - And if you will say: It is revealed and known to the Omnipresent what he intended, whether for good or for ill. And one can answer that even when he intends [it] for good — so that it will not burn quickly, and the homeowner will be able to rescue [it] in the meantime — nevertheless, he is liable according to the laws of Heaven, for he ought to have been careful and to have considered that a loss might come to him through this.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:22:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא הויא לה תחלתו בפשיעה וסופו באונס קמ"ל דכולהו פשיעה היא - ק"ק, דה"ל למימר: "מהו דתימא כולה אונס הוא", וכגון שנעל כל כך יפה שאינה יכולה לצאת אלא בחתירה; קמשמע לן דפושע הוא אצל חתירה, שהניחה בחמה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:22:1.english: Lest you say that this is [a case of] "initially through negligence and ultimately by accident," [the Mishnah] teaches us that [the] entire [damage] is negligence - It is somewhat difficult, for [the Gemara] should have said: "Lest you say that it is entirely by accident" — [i.e.,] in a case where he locked [the pen] so well that [the animal] could not get out except by tunneling — [and the Mishnah] teaches us that he is [considered] negligent with respect to tunneling, since he left it in the sun.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:2:1.hebrew: אילימא דמטיא ליה ברוח מצויה בדיני אדם נמי ליחייב - וא"ת: כיון שאין חילוק בין מקרב דבר אצל האש ובין מקרב האש אצל הדבר, אמאי אמרינן בפרק כל הנשרפין (סנהדרין דף עז. ושם): "כפתו במקום שסוף חמה או צינה לבא — פטור"? ליחייב למ"ד אשו משום חציו, וכן כפתו לפני ארי! וי"ל: דודאי אי כפתו והביאו במקום שסוף חמה או צינה לבא או ארי — חייב, אבל התם מיירי שכפתו במקום שהיה ולא הזיזו ממקומו, ולא הוי מצמצם, הואיל והחמה והצינה והארי אין עליו בשעת כפיתה. וההיא דאתקיל עליה בדקא דמיא, אפילו כפתו והביאו שם ואח"כ אתקיל — פטור, דדמי לזורק חץ ותריס בידו, ואפילו קדם הוא ונטלו — פטור. וא"ת: ההיא דהשיך בו את הנחש, דפטור למ"ד מעצמו הוא מכיש, אמאי פטור? לפי מה שפירש בשמעתין דפי פרה (דף כג:) ששם ידו לתוך פיו והשיך, ליחייב משום אשו, דודאי הנחש יזיק האדם! וי"ל: דשאני התם, שאין הארס עדיין בעולם:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:2:1.english: If we say that it reaches it in a typical wind, let him also be liable under human laws - And if you ask: Since there is no distinction between bringing an object near the fire and bringing the fire near the object, why do we say in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaNisrafin (Sanhedrin 77a and there): "[If] one tied him up in a place where the sun or cold will eventually come, he is exempt"? Let him be liable according to the one who says [that liability for] his fire is due to [it being considered] his arrows, and similarly [in the case where] he tied him up before a lion! And one can answer: Certainly, if he tied him up and brought him to a place where the sun or cold will eventually come, or [before] a lion, he is liable; however, there [the Gemara] is dealing with [a case] where he tied him up in the place where he [already] was and did not move him from his place, and it is not [a case of] confining [him to danger], since the sun, the cold, and the lion are not upon him at the time of the tying. And [as for] that [case] where a burst of water came upon him — even if he tied him up and brought him there and afterward [the water] burst [upon him], he is exempt, for it is similar to one who shoots an arrow while [the target] has a shield in his hand, where even if he went ahead and removed it, he is exempt. And if you ask: [In] that [case] where he caused a snake to bite him, where he is exempt according to the one who says [the snake] bites of its own accord, why is he exempt? According to what [the Gemara] explained in our sugya of "the mouth of the cow" (23b), that he placed his hand into its mouth and caused [it] to bite, let him be liable on account of "his fire," since the snake will certainly harm the person! And one can answer: There it is different, because the venom is not yet in the world:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:4:1.hebrew: ממונא בעי לשלומי - וכי תימא: פטור מדיני אדם משום דלא ידעי' שהם עדי שקר — מ"מ, כיון שאם היינו יודעין שהם עדות שקר משלם, אין שייך למיתני "פטור מדיני אדם":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:4:1.english: He is required to pay money - And if you say [that he is] exempt according to human laws because we do not know that they are false witnesses — nevertheless, since if we knew that they were false testimony he would pay, it is not appropriate to teach [in the baraita]: "exempt according to human laws."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:4:2.hebrew: אלא לחבריה - כגון שאין לחבריה מה לשלם, או שהלך למדינת הים, או כגון שאין אנו יודעים שהם עדי שקר. ודוקא שוכר, אבל אמר — פטור מדיני שמים, דסבור שלא ישמעו לו; דאין נראה לומר דנקט "שוכר" לאשמועינן דאפי' שוכר פטור מדיני אדם, שאין זה שום חידוש, ולקמן לא עביד צריכותא אלא מדיני שמים. ועוד, דבפירקין תנן (דף נט:): "השולח את הבערה ביד חש"ו פטור מדיני אדם וחייב בדיני שמים; שלח ביד פקח — הפקח חייב", משמע דשולח פטור אף מדיני שמים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:4:2.english: Rather, [he hired them] for [the benefit of] another - [This is a case] such as where his friend has nothing with which to pay, or where he went overseas, or such as where we do not know that they are false witnesses. And specifically one who hires [them is liable under Heavenly law], whereas if he merely told [them to testify falsely], he is exempt [even] from Heavenly law, because he assumed they would not listen to him; for it does not seem [correct] to say that [the baraita] used the term "one who hires" to teach us that even one who hires is exempt from human law, as that is no novelty at all, and later on [the Gemara] only makes a tzerikhuta [to explain the necessity of the cases] with respect to Heavenly law. Furthermore, in our chapter we learned in a Mishnah (59b): "One who sends a fire in the hand of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor is exempt from human law and liable under Heavenly law; if he sent it in the hand of a mentally competent person, the mentally competent person is liable" — which implies that the sender is exempt even from Heavenly law.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:5:1.hebrew: פשיטא אם לא יגיד וכו' - וא"ת: ה"מ כשעבר על שבועתו, כדכתיב "ושמעה קול אלה"? וי"ל: דה"ק קרא — כשעובר בדבר שאם לא יגיד היה נושא עון, אז יביא קרבן שבועה; אבל בלא שבועה נמי איכא נשיאות עון, כדמוכח במתני' באחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין דף לז:). ודוקא בב"ד, דכשאומרים "אין אנו יודעים להעיד" שוב אינם יכולין להעיד, דכיון שהגיד שוב אינו חוזר ומגיד — והיינו "אם לא יגיד" דקרא; אבל חוץ לב"ד אין לחוש, שיכול לחזור ולהעיד:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:5:1.english: It is obvious: "If he does not utter it," etc. - And if you ask: This [liability] applies only when he violated his oath, as it is written, "and hears the voice of an adjuration"? One can answer that this is what the verse is saying: When he transgresses in a matter where, if he does not utter [his testimony], he would bear iniquity, then he must bring an oath-offering; but even without an oath, there is also bearing of iniquity, as is proven in the Mishnah in [the chapter entitled] Echad Dinei Mamonot (Sanhedrin 37b). And [this applies] specifically in court, for when they say, "We do not know [anything] to testify," they can no longer testify afterward, since once [a witness] has stated [his testimony], he cannot retract and state [something else] — and this is [the meaning of] "if he does not utter it" in the verse; however, outside of court there is no concern, since he can still go back and testify.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:7:1.hebrew: העושה מלאכה במי חטאת - עד שלא נתן האפר, כדתניא במס' פרה (פ"ד מ"ד): "פרה נפסלת במלאכה עד שתעשה אפר, והמלאכה פוסלת במים עד שישים האפר לתוכה". ובספרי יליף מקרא: יכול אף קדשן? ת"ל "למשמרת למי נדה" — ולא שכבר מי נדה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:7:1.english: One who performs labor with water of purification - [This applies] before one has placed the ash [in the water], as it is taught in Tractate Parah (4:4): "A heifer is disqualified through labor until it is made into ash, and labor disqualifies the water until one places the ash into it." And in the Sifrei, [the Tanna] derives [this] from a verse: One might think [that labor disqualifies it] even after one has sanctified it? Therefore, the verse states, "to be kept for water of purification" — and not that which is already water of purification.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:7:2.hebrew: פטור מדיני אדם - בפ' הניזקין (גיטין נג.), פריך מיניה למ"ד היזק שאין ניכר שמיה היזק:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 56a:7:2.english: Exempt according to human laws - In the chapter [entitled] HaNizakin (Gittin 53a), [the Gemara] raises an objection from it against the one who says [that] damage that is not evident is considered damage.
